Welcome
Bassett House School is an outstanding co-educational school in Notting Hill for girls and boys aged 2-11. We are a smaller school and so Bassett pupils create a palpable feeling of a school that is welcoming with a big heart; it is caring and full of charm.
Welcome from the Head
There’s something quietly – yet confidently – wonderful about Bassett House. You sense it the moment you walk through our door: it is not in grand statements or a polished prospectus, but in the everyday, genuine warmth of our school family.
We are a school with a big heart. You hear this in the laughter of children who feel at home, and you see this in the genuine relationships that underpin everything we do. And, thankfully, academic-excellence and kindness are not mutually exclusive in 2026.

Head’s Welcome
Welcome to Bassett House School.
When you walk through the doors of Bassett House, you will no doubt understand why the school is known as a small school with a rather large heart.
It is my pleasure to be the Head of Bassett House, a thriving and successful school where the children lie at the core of all that we do and this is wholly evident in the genuine relationships the children form with each other and the staff.
Founded in 1947, and one of Notting Hill’s oldest Prep Schools, Bassett House has successfully continued to evolve and build an excellent reputation in the locality and beyond. Our teachers know all of the children incredibly well – we know their strengths, their potentials, their aspirations and their characters, all underpinned by our founding motto, ‘Be the best you can be’.
In order for you to experience what makes Bassett House so special, please do arrange a visit to the school where you can see the children in action.
Mr Pádraic Fahy Head of Bassett House School
Where next?

Head’s Welcome
Welcome to Bassett House School.
When you walk through the doors of Bassett House, you will no doubt understand why the school is known as a small school with a rather large heart.
It is my pleasure to be the Head of Bassett House, a thriving and successful school where the children lie at the core of all that we do and this is wholly evident in the genuine relationships the children form with each other and the staff.
Founded in 1947, and one of Notting Hill’s oldest Prep Schools, Bassett House has successfully continued to evolve and build an excellent reputation in the locality and beyond. Our teachers know all of the children incredibly well – we know their strengths, their potentials, their aspirations and their characters, all underpinned by our founding motto, ‘Be the best you can be’.
In order for you to experience what makes Bassett House so special, please do arrange a visit to the school where you can see the children in action.

Performing & Creative Arts
Performing Arts
At Bassett House, we believe that every child is a performer. We encourage performance in music and drama for the self-expression it gives our pupils, to promote teamwork, as a means of building confidence and to cultivate public speaking, singing and instrumental skills. We aim to recognise each pupil’s strengths and talents and to develop these to their fullest potential.
All our pupils perform. Whether in class assemblies, nativity plays, whole-year theatre productions, our Harvest Festival and Christmas carol service, young musicians’ assemblies, orchestra, choirs, instrument ensembles, Eurhythmics dance movement lessons, or even carolling for tourists on the Portobello Road (in aid of charity). The emphasis is on participation, not perfection.
We study music in the curriculum through movement, composition, Drama, dance and improvisation and look to engender a lifelong love of music through exposure to a breadth of musical genres. We also offer drama and performing arts clubs.
Art
We consider every child to be an artist. We encourage creativity and self-expression through a variety of media, including painting, drawing, sculpture, and digital art. We also explore different cultural and historical connections, as well as contemporary references. We celebrate the artistic and cultural riches on our doorstep by taking trips to London galleries, holding a Royal Academy life drawing workshop for our older children and visiting local professional art studios. Each week one child’s effort is recognised by our Artist of the Week award and we celebrate the whole school’s creativity in our Annual Art Week Showcase. We are very proud that our alumni have won art scholarships to prestigious senior schools.
Music
We believe that music is an essential part of a well-rounded education. We offer a wide range of musical opportunities for our pupils, including:
We also have a number of visiting music teachers who offer tuition in a variety of instruments.

Prep Curriculum
Co-educational environment
Our children benefit from being in a co-educational environment where girls and boys learn from each other, both academically and socially.
English
Alongside encouraging reading, or being read to at home, we expose pupils to a wide variety of stories, genres and authors to foster a love of reading, enable the children to gain a deeper appreciation of different texts and to translate that into their own writing. Events that bring English literature to life punctuate the calendar: our inter-house poetry competition, book week, trips to see plays on the London stage, drama workshops and visits by published authors. Bassett House School children leave us as confident and articulate communicators, well able to use the written word to persuade, entertain, amuse, educate or enlighten their readers.
Phonics
We use a ‘teach, practise, apply’ lesson approach aimed to cater for all learning styles. We ensure children gain a secure understanding of phonics right from age 3 by reading with each child every day through to the end of Form 2 and allowing them to progress at their own pace. There is a phonics coordinator who oversees the teaching of phonics within the Preschool and Reception year groups.
Mathematics
We encourage the children to understand each mathematical concept they encounter, so that skills and knowledge are embedded and consolidated in ability-boosting building blocks. Maths mastery is achieved through the use of concrete resources and visual aids; using mathematical terminology consistently throughout the school; tackling the same concepts from different angles and adapted to different learning styles, and aiming for depth of understanding over breadth of coverage.
Science
We use ‘hands on’ and interactive learning to develop key scientific skills across a varied curriculum: dissecting a lamb’s heart, watching eggs hatch in a classroom incubator, hunting for invertebrates in the park, ‘exploding’ volcanoes by mixing vinegar with bicarbonate of soda and creating electrical circuits are all part of a Bassett House School scientist’s life. We ‘scaffold’ learning up through the school so that the children consolidate previous learning and add depth of understanding as they progress. We also emphasise the importance and relevance of science by exploring the discoveries, impacts and real-world applications of famous scientists and inventors.
Each week a child is awarded Scientist of the Week and annually we have a whole-school STEAM week, promoting Science, Technology, Engineering, Art and Maths. We also take our science quest elsewhere: a much-anticipated Bassett House School thrill is our Form 5 trip to stay overnight in the Science Museum.
Geography
We explore a range of case studies from the local area to the countries in the wider world, creating an understanding of human and physical geography.
Commencing from the start of our pupil’s educational journey, we might head out with iPads to photograph buildings in our neighbourhood to better understand our local environment, we use field work and outdoor learning to enhance the children’s understanding of different geographical processes. To further embed this, we might be looking at river courses in Suffolk, thinking about the topography of Salisbury Plain on a trip to Stonehenge, pondering urban planning in York or finding examples of coastal erosion in the Isle of Wight.
History
Our emphasis is on innovative teaching with cross-curricular links to ensure that the children not only learn content but also skills, including historical enquiry, developing a sense of chronology, and critically evaluating and debating historical accounts. The children are given a firm foundation in the chronology of a topic as well as exciting trips to provide context, drama to encourage empathy and research projects to promote independence of thought. Activities that bring the past to life for our Bassett historians include dressing up as Victorian servants at Gunnersbury Park Museum, experiencing the sights and smells of the Vikings at York’s Jorvik Centre, creating their own Greek temples or Egyptian sarcophagi, exploring Stonehenge and Danebury Hill Fort, discovering the dynasty of Victoria and Albert at Osborne House on the Isle of Wight, and following in medieval footsteps by climbing York Minster tower.
Religious Education
We enhance pupils’ awareness and understanding of the variety of religions and beliefs, teachings and practices, as well as of the influence of religion on individuals, families, communities and cultures. Lessons might include songs, stories, religious art and artefacts and, on special occasions, food and rituals. We visit centres of different worship in order to give the children some real-world insights into different faiths and we are fortunate to have parents willing to share their own religious practice by visiting us and telling us about it. Children from different religious backgrounds attend Bassett House and we celebrate our religious diversity by observing all the major festivals.
PSHE
We take a consistent approach to teaching important moral values throughout the school and provide a safe and nurturing environment in which children are free to express their ideas and beliefs while learning to respect cultural, social and religious differences. We engage our pupils not only in our internal school community via our thriving house system, Citizenship Council and Eco Council, but also in the wider world by looking at current affairs, supporting local charities and inviting speakers such as police officers, doctors, nurses, firefighters and politicians.
Computing
In timetabled computing lessons, from Reception onwards, children are encouraged to explore technology, solve problems and think logically. We aim to produce competent, confident and creative users of information and communication technology. Our children become digitally literate and learn how to use the internet safely, respectfully and responsibly. Most importantly, at Bassett House School, computer technology is one of the tools used to deliver the whole curriculum, whether creating a PowerPoint presentation on the life of a Roman slave, delivering a quiz on the human digestive system or racing one another at times tables. All our classrooms are equipped with iMacs and interactive whiteboards (connected to teacher iPads) and we have banks of iPads, MacBook Air laptops and Google Chromebooks available for class use.
French
The emphasis is on understanding French through immersion, developing vocabulary through fun games and songs, using French language applications to support learning and gaining confidence in adopting the correct pronunciation. We participate in French competitions with other schools and take trips to see French films at the Ciné Lumière. By Form 6, our children spend a week at a French château at which the staff speak nothing but French. We aim for Bassett House School pupils to progress to their senior schools with a can-do enthusiasm for learning foreign languages, as well as a grasp of basic French.
Latin
We focus on bringing Latin back to life using comic strips and songs, acting and storytelling (at times treating Latin as though it were a modern language). We look at classical history and civilisations and, during our Form 4 trip to York, explore a legionnaire’s life in the Roman army. We also celebrate the Bassett House Latin motto, quisque pro sua parte, which we translate as ‘for each, the best!’: everyone should receive all that they need to excel.

Prep
Bassett House Prep School
Bassett House Prep School is home to boys and girls aged 4 to 11, in the heart of Notting Hill, West London. From Reception through to Year 6, our pupils build on the confident, curious start they made in our Early Years, growing into resilient, well-rounded learners ready for the move to senior school at 11+ – all within the same warm, close-knit school with the big heart that Bassett House has had since 1947. Children can start in nursery and transition through, so it really starts at 2.
Life at our Prep School
What sets Bassett House apart isn’t a single big idea – it’s the accumulation of small ones. We’re a genuinely small school, which means every child is known individually, by name and by nature, not just by year group. Children move from Early Years into Prep as part of one continuous journey, not a fresh start, so the transition into Year 2 feels familiar rather than daunting.
As part of the wider Dukes Education family, we’re also able to draw on shared best practice, training and resources from across a network of like-minded schools – without ever losing the small-school feel that makes Bassett House what it is. Academic excellence and kindness are not mutually exclusive here; we hold both at once, every day.
Curriculum at a glance
4 to 11 years (Reception –6)
Montessori-founded roots carried forward from Early Years, a mastery approach in mathematics, and hands-on, practical teaching in science
11+ entrance preparation, destination senior schools
French, Latin, Computing, Art and PSHE, alongside core English, Maths, Science, History, Geography and RE
Non-selective entry point, with ongoing formative assessment rather than early high-stakes testing
Our maths teaching follows a mastery model – prioritising real depth of understanding over racing through content, using concrete resources and visual aids so every child genuinely embeds each concept. Science is taught hands-on wherever possible, through practical, memorable experiments, and English is built around developing imagination and vocabulary through a genuinely wide range of texts and authors.
Pastoral care and wellbeing
We believe children develop well when they feel secure, happy and valued – and that shapes everything from our house system, which brings pupils together in mixed teams to build teamwork and belonging, to our buddy system, which pairs older children with younger ones during moments of transition. Every child also has their own way of raising a concern, however big or small, whenever they need to. Read more on our Pastoral Care page.
Academic success and destination schools
Our Prep pupils consistently go on to leading senior schools at 11+ – a moment we celebrate as a school every year, most recently in Celebrating Our Year 6 Success at 11+. Read more about our approach to academic achievement on our Academic Success page, and see where recent leavers have gone on to our 11+ & Destination Schools page.
Enrichment beyond the classroom
Life at Bassett House extends well beyond the timetable. Our enrichment programme spans performing and creative arts, PE and sport, a wide range of after-school clubs, and trips that bring learning to life outside the classroom – building confidence, teamwork and genuine enthusiasm alongside academic progress. Explore Performing & Creative Arts, PE & Sport, Clubs and Trips.
Frequently Asked Questions
What age range does Bassett House Prep School cover?
Bassett House Prep School is for children aged 4 to 11, from Reception through to Year 6, continuing directly on from our Early Years provision.
Where is Bassett House Prep School located?
We’re based at 60 Bassett Road, London W10 6JP, in the heart of Notting Hill, West London.
Is Bassett House Prep School co-educational?
Yes. Bassett House is fully co-educational throughout the Prep years – read more on our Co-Educational Learning page.
How do children join the Prep School from Early Years?
Children move from our Early Years provision into Prep at age 4 (Reception) as part of one continuous journey through the school, rather than starting afresh at a new school.
What senior schools do Bassett House pupils go on to?
Our pupils consistently receive offers to leading senior schools at 11+. See our 11+ & Destination Schools page for more.
How do I book a visit or arrange a tour?
You can book a private tour or attend a Stay and Play session via our Visit Us page.
What is the admissions process for Bassett House Prep School?
Our Admissions team will guide you through every step, from your first enquiry to securing a place. Get in touch for a full walkthrough of the process.
Where next?

Bassett House School is part of the Dukes Education family of schools and educators, brought together by a common purpose: to give children the foundations for an extraordinary life.
We create clusters of nurseries and schools in village locations to ensure that families can enjoy the option of an all-through education journey with Dukes Education within their local area.
Continuity and Confidence
As students prepare to transition from prep school to senior school at Year 7, our guaranteed entry policy offers a seamless progression within the Dukes family of senior schools, subject only to the availability of a place and a child’s ability to thrive in the ethos and curriculum, and without the need to sit traditional school entrance exams such as the 11+.
Guaranteed Placement, Tailored Support
Dukes Education supports each child’s journey to senior school, working with families to find the right school; one that matches their unique strengths and aspirations.
Our commitment to providing a guaranteed place at a Dukes Education senior school allows students to focus on their personal and academic development instead of spending precious time preparing for school entrance exams and the added pressure that entails.
For families applying to selective senior schools, our prep schools provide thorough guidance, tailored 11+ exam preparation and exceptional pastoral support to ensure that every student is ready to perform at their best.
This approach ensures a confident and smooth transition to senior school for all children, nurturing lifelong learners within the supportive framework of Dukes Education.
Early acceptance
If a family decides their child will not sit the 11+ entrance test, we are usually able to confirm acceptance to a Dukes senior school in Year 5. Early acceptance offers families peace of mind, allowing children to enjoy their final years at prep school and focus on a positive transition to senior school.

pageCache.pageTitle: What is a Prep School? | Bassett House School
pageCache.text:
What Is A Prep School?
What is a Prep School?
A prep school – short for “preparatory school” – is a UK independent school that prepares children for entry to senior school, typically through the 11+ or 13+ entrance exams. Most prep schools are fee-paying, offer smaller class sizes than the state sector, and introduce specialist subject teaching earlier than a typical primary school.
How a prep school differs from a primary school
While a state primary school takes children from Reception through to Year 6 as part of the free state education system, a prep school is an independent, fee-paying alternative built around the same core purpose: preparing children academically, socially and personally for the next stage of their education. Prep schools typically offer smaller class sizes, specialist teaching in subjects like art, music, French and PE from an earlier age, and a curriculum specifically designed with senior school entry – and its exams – in mind.
What age range do prep schools cover?
There’s no single fixed age range across all UK prep schools – it varies from school to school. Many prep schools take children from age 7 or 8 through to 11 or 13, while others, like Bassett House, offer a fully continuous journey from Nursery age right through to Year 6, so a child never has to change schools during their entire prep-school years.
What does prep school life look like at Bassett House?
At Bassett House, we’re a co-educational prep school for boys and girls aged 2 to 11, based in Notting Hill, West London. Children join us as early as Nursery and can stay with us right through to Year 6 and their move to senior school at 11+ – one continuous, familiar journey rather than several separate transitions.
Our teaching philosophy is Montessori-founded in the early years and mastery-based through Prep, built around genuine understanding rather than simply covering content quickly. Every class is fully co-educational, and every child is known individually within a small, close-knit school community. Read more about our teaching philosophy and co-educational learning at Bassett House.
Frequently Asked Questions
What does "prep school" actually mean?
“Prep school” is short for “preparatory school” – an independent school that prepares children for entry to senior school, usually via the 11+ or 13+ entrance exams.
What age do children start prep school?
This varies by school – some start at 7 or 8, others earlier. At Bassett House, children can join from age 2 in our Nursery and continue right through to Year 6.
What is the difference between a prep school and a private school?
A prep school is a type of private (independent) school, specifically focused on the years leading up to senior school entry, rather than a separate category of education.
Do children need to sit an exam to leave a prep school?
Most prep school pupils sit entrance exams – commonly known as the 11+ or 13+ – to move on to their chosen senior school, and prep schools typically build their curriculum with this preparation in mind.
Is Bassett House a prep school?
Yes. Bassett House is a co-educational prep school in Notting Hill for children aged 2 to 11, offering a continuous journey from Nursery through to Year 6 and 11+ preparation.
How do I find out about fees at Bassett House?
Full details on our termly fees are available on our Fees page.
How can I visit Bassett House to see prep school life for myself?
You can book a private tour or attend an open event via our Visit Us page – we’d love to show you around.

An Independent Prep School in North Kensington
A small school with a big heart, we have called this cosy corner of West London home since 1947.
Tucked among quiet residential streets between Kensington Memorial Park and Ladbroke Grove, Bassett House School is a co-educational independent prep school in North Kensington and the Notting Hill area, welcoming children aged 2 to 11. Our motto ‘For each the best’ (Latin: Quisque pro sua parte) perfectly encapsulates our dedication to creating an academically rich, yet welcoming, space for our pupils – a home away from home where they can achieve their full individual potential.
Where We Are Located
Bassett House is split between two facilities:
In addition to these two sites, we have access to St Helen’s Church, just around the corner, whose hall and grounds we use for assembly, PE, and outdoor space. Our pupils are also within walking distance of the Westway Sports Centre for sports and extra-curricular activities, and they use the fantastic outdoor play area at Kensington Memorial Park at break and lunchtime.
Virtual Tour
Navigate around the school by using the tool on the menu bar at the bottom right of the tour. You can also use the arrows on the same bar to scroll through the scenes.
Key
Main building
Formerly a large family residence, the school’s main building was built in the late 19th century in the leafy streets of North Kensington. 60 Bassett Road was purpose re-built in 2001, whilst holding true to the Victorian architectural principles of large, bright and airy rooms. It now houses 10 classrooms and an outside play area. Our pupils in the Upper Prep years are based here.
St Helen’s Church
The school’s premises also include the large hall at St Helen’s Church just round the corner, providing a professional stage and assembly hall/gymnasium, three classrooms, a custom-built kitchen and a garden play area.
Bassett Bear House
Bassett Bear House is our newly renovated state-of-the-art home for Early Years. It houses our Nursery School (aged 3+) and Reception (aged 4+) in three light and spacious classrooms and provides a large interactive learning zone. We have a basement music/drama studio for the use of the whole school, together with smaller group tutorial spaces.
Attend a stay and play
Kensington Memorial Park
Kensington Memorial Park is a short 5 minute walk from the school building. Children visit the park multiple times per week, at both break and lunch time.
Read more about the park here
Westway Sports Centre
There are state of the art facilities at the Westway Sports Centre, including the largest climbing wall in London, an LTA Accredited tennis performance centre, eight outdoor floodlit 3G football pitches and floodlit cricket lanes.
Areas We Serve
Most families who come through our admissions portal live within walking, cycling, or scooting distance, across North Kensington, Notting Hill, and Kensal Rise. Many more travel in from Kensal Green, Queen’s Park, Maida Vale and West Kilburn, using the bus routes and Underground stations on our doorstep.
Wherever you are moving from, our position just off Ladbroke Grove puts us within easy reach of most of West London’s family neighbourhoods, without the premium of a Notting Hill Gate or Holland Park postcode.
Getting to Bassett House
Bassett Road is well connected by Underground, Overground and bus, with several options within a short walk:
Latimer Road (Circle, Hammersmith & City)
Ladbroke Grove (Circle, Hammersmith & City)
Route 7 and 316 at St Charles Square
Route 295 at Cambridge Gardens
Routes 23, 52, 70, 228 at Ladbroke Grove Station
Bus (Nursery and Reception)
Route 7 and 316 at St Charles Square
Route 295 at Cambridge Gardens
Routes 23, 52, 70, 228 at Ladbroke Grove Station
Given the walk from the nearest stations, many families choose to cycle, scoot or take the bus. Bassett Road sits within a controlled parking zone, so on-street parking is limited; please be considerate of our neighbours if you do need to drive.
Local Area and Community
Bassett House sits close to the northern reach of Portobello Road, with its market stalls and independent shops, and a short walk from the colourful shopfronts of Golborne Road. Green space is close by too: our pupils walk to Kensington Memorial Park for regular recreation, and games lessons take place at the nearby Westway Sports Centre.
Further north, Kensal Green Cemetery and the canal towpath at Little Venice give older pupils a taste of a quieter, leafier side of the city, while the murals and community gardens around Meanwhile Gardens reflect the creative, close-knit character of the neighbourhood Bassett House has called home for more than 75 years.
A Shared History: Sylvia Rentoul and the Wider Dukes Family
Sylvia Rentoul founded Bassett House in 1947, opening the school with just six pupils at a time, when children were still widely expected to be seen and not heard. Sylvia’s approach was different: she believed children should be encouraged to express themselves, that learning should be both supportive and genuinely challenging, and that teaching should always respond to the individual needs of the child in front of you – ideas that were ahead of their time in 1947 and still shape how we teach today.
That same philosophy travelled with the family. In 1993, inspired by their mother’s vision, Sylvia’s sons founded Orchard House School in Chiswick, and the two schools have shared a close bond ever since, alongside Prospect House School in Putney. In February 2020, all three schools joined the wider Dukes Education family, opening up new opportunities for collaboration while each kept its own distinct, close-knit community. Bassett House is proud to be where that story began.
Nursery and Prep in North Kensington
Bassett House Nursery welcomes children from age 2 into a warm, Montessori-informed start to school life. Families searching for a nursery in North Kensington or Notting Hill can book a visit and see it for themselves.
Prep school begins in Reception (age 4), another natural entry point, and children move through Bassett House and stay with us through Year 6 (age 11). After Bassett House, our pupils go on to the best senior schools in the country. We may be a small school, but our results speak for themselves. Some of the schools our pupils have been accepted to, both with and without scholarships, include:
St Paul’s Girls
Magdalen College School, Oxford
St James Girls
Latymer Upper
Godolphin and Latymer
The Harrodian
Ibstock Place

Notting Hill and Ealing

Frequently Asked Questions
Where is Bassett House School located?
Bassett House School is at 60 Bassett Road, London W10 6JP, in North Kensington, close to Ladbroke Grove and a short walk from St Helen’s Church, whose hall we use for assembly and PE.
Which areas does Bassett House serve?
Families join us from across North Kensington, Notting Hill, Kensal Rise, Kensal Green, Queen’s Park, Maida Vale and West Kilburn, along with some families travelling in from further across West London.
Is Bassett House close to Portobello Road?
Yes. The school sits close to the northern end of Portobello Road and is a short walk from Golborne Road, both well known for their markets and independent shops.
How do I get to Bassett House by public transport?
The nearest Underground stations are Ladbroke Grove and Latimer Road, both on the Circle and Hammersmith & City lines and around a 10-minute walk away. Kensal Green, on the Bakerloo line and London Overground, is a similar distance in the other direction. Buses 7, 23, 52, 70, 295 and 316 all stop close to the school.
Is there parking at Bassett House?
On-street parking near Bassett Road is limited because of the local controlled parking zone, so we encourage families to walk, cycle, or take the bus where possible. Please be considerate of our neighbours if you do need to drive.
Is Bassett House School the same as Notting Hill Prep?
No. Notting Hill Prep is a separate independent prep school on Lancaster Road, also in Notting Hill, and the two schools are not owned by the same group. Bassett House is based on Bassett Road in North Kensington and has been an independent school since 1947.
What is Bassett House's connection to Orchard House and Prospect House?
Bassett House is the founding school of a small family of schools. Our founder’s sons went on to establish Orchard House School in Chiswick in 1993, and we later joined Prospect House School in Putney and the wider Dukes Education family in 2020, though each school keeps its own distinct community and site.
What age range does Bassett House accept?
Bassett House welcomes children from age 2 in our Nursery through Year 6 (age 11), all on our single site on Bassett Road.
Is Bassett House suitable for families relocating to North Kensington or Notting Hill?
Yes. Our position just off Ladbroke Grove, close to good transport links, makes Bassett House a natural choice for families relocating to West London, and our Admissions team is happy to help with timing and overseas applications.

The pastoral care is excellent too – there are off-timetable enrichment sessions, an in-house life coach and peace lilies (which, according to NASA, purify the air) placed in every classroom. Recent leavers have won scholarships to Latymer Upper and City of London School for Girls, and, reportedly, the only complaint pupils have is that the school day ends too early”.
Hear from our children
Bassett House’s teachers are wonderful because they give everybody a chance to shine.
There are wonderful opportunities for all pupils and there are fantastic trips.
At Bassett House, no matter what you are good at, the teachers will support you throughout your time here.

Hear from our parents
We love watching how our children have developed so beautifully at Bassett House. They are confident and self-aware. The school provides everything we could ask for.
Parent of children in Year 1 and Year 5.
Our son has been able to try so many activities. The Bassett House ethos of ‘First Attempt in Learning’ has become a part of our home-life too.
Parent of a child in Year 3
The teachers have made a solid effort to ensure that there were no gaps in learning when we moved from a State School. We are continually impressed by their dedication to the students.

Pastoral Care
No child has any doubt their teachers and staff will listen to their issues. Each child has a personal ‘Pupil Plan’ where pupils can note any personal notes or worries so teachers can monitor their happiness and well-being. There is also a ‘worry box’ in the hall where children can post any concerns.
Our buddy system helps newcomers through their early days, and we encourage older children to mentor younger pupils, instilling a sense of responsibility. Our growth mindset philosophy supports and inspires children if they are having difficulty sharing or managing a friendship issue.
We encourage older children to mentor younger pupils, instilling a sense of responsibility.
We invite them to one of our weekly ‘communication stations’ where they can practise strategies or try re-framing their perception of the issue. They learn emotional and social matters are not fixed and can be an opportunity for personal growth.
The school’s house system encourages teamwork and a competitive spirit, allowing children to celebrate their own success as well as the achievement of others. Whole school events and charitable activities foster a sense of pride in belonging to a wider community.
Where next?

Academic Success
Our pupils are privileged to benefit from academically achieving to exceptionally high standards.
Our children go on to the best senior schools in London. During their time with us, they benefit from a curriculum crafted by specialist teachers and best pedagogical practice implemented throughout the school. But more importantly, they are resilient, curious and confident in their intellect and cultural appreciation.
Our pupils have a love of learning embedded within them during their time with us, and with the utilisation of Carol Dweck’s growth-mindset approach, they show resilience by attempting everything without the fear of failure. Failure doesn’t exist at Bassett House. Here, we see it as a first attempt at learning.
Passion for teaching is displayed throughout the school. Bassett House School teachers are selected by way of a rigorous recruitment process, with an underlying focus on their personal can-do attitudes towards their classroom management and lesson structures. Our pupils thrive in these conditions and are confident, considered individuals who have strong foundations for their bright futures.
Where next?

Clubs
Extra-curricular clubs offer a wealth of benefits for children. They provide opportunities to develop new skills and interests outside of the traditional classroom setting, fostering a sense of curiosity and enthusiasm.
Participation in these activities can significantly boost confidence, as children discover hidden talents and excel in areas they may not have previously explored. A child who once struggled with maths may well excel once they discover they have a hidden talent for something else.
Bassett House School offers a wide spectrum of activities that encourage self-expression and the development of talents outside the classroom, allowing children to explore new subjects, build friendships and connect with peers who share similar interests.
Weekly clubs include art, animation, coding, cooking, chess, drama, fencing, horse riding, martial arts, netball, swimming and yoga. Visiting music teachers offer individual music tuition and pupils can join the school chamber choir, senior and junior choirs and instrumental ensembles including a rock band!
If your child is a budding journalist, they have the chance to develop their reporting skills via our radio station club, ‘Bassett Radio’, and through our newspaper club ‘Bassett’s Big News’.
